one_liner: AVX-512 IFMA int64/uint64-to-decimal conversion; 2.8x std::to_chars throughput on 12-19 digit integers, slower at 1-4 digits.
what_it_does: Converts one 64-bit signed or unsigned integer to ASCII decimal digits: size_t simditoa::to_chars(value, char* buf) writes the digits (no terminator) and returns the length; the caller must supply at least MAX_DIGITS + 1 = 21 bytes. It also exposes to_chars_heterogeneous and to_chars_homogeneous (same output, different code paths) and a uint64-only to_chars_batch that samples 1% of the input to pick a variant. The interface differs from std::to_chars: there is no end pointer, no std::to_chars_result or errc, no base argument, and only 64-bit types.
how_it_is_fast: It implements Champagne Gareau and Lemire's method (arXiv:2604.26019): the value is broadcast into eight 64-bit lanes, vpmadd52lo multiplies it by the constants floor(2^52/10^k) to get each digit's fractional remainder, and vpmadd52hi multiplies by 10 to pull out the ASCII digit, so 8 digits come out in parallel with no division or lookup table. 16-digit values run two such kernels on the high and low 8-digit halves and gather the bytes with a VBMI vpermt2b permute; 17-20 digit values add a 4-digit scalar tail. The heterogeneous variant uses one 3-way branch plus masked stores (length from a branchless clz-table digit count), and the homogeneous variant uses a 20-way switch with unmasked 16-byte stores.
when_to_use: Serializing many large integers (IDs, nanosecond timestamps, Snowflake IDs, counters of 12-19 digits) on Ice Lake or later Intel, or Zen 4 or later AMD, built with -mavx512ifma -mavx512vbmi: about 186-190M ints/s vs std::to_chars 59-100M on FIXED:12/16/19 (Xeon 8481C).
Mixed-length positive inputs where branch prediction fails: on LOG_HEAVY (40-63 bit values) 135.3M vs 39.6M ints/s for std::to_chars (3.4x) and vs 74.9M for yy_itoa.

Bulk output of same-length values (fixed-width IDs): to_chars_homogeneous reaches 295.7M ints/s at 12 and 16 digits, and to_chars_batch selects it automatically when at least 95% of a 1% sample share one length.
Hot JSON, CSV or log writers that already provide at least 21 bytes of slack at the write cursor.
when_not_to_use: Mostly short numbers (1-4 digits): the SIMD setup cost is constant, so the default path is slower than std::to_chars at 1 digit (267.3M vs 402.5M ints/s) and 4 digits (225.4M vs 319.6M), and far behind jeaiii (1,011M) and fmt (986M) at 1 digit.
Random-sign signed data: the negative-value branch mispredicts, and throughput drops from 186.2M (UNIFORM_POS) to 101.2M ints/s on full-range int64, where yy_itoa is faster (128.6M).

Portable binaries or generic x86-64 builds: implementation choice is compile-time only (no runtime CPU dispatch). The default CMake build without the AVX-512 flags silently gives the scalar fallback, which was never benchmarked, and a build with the flags crashes with an illegal instruction on CPUs without IFMA/VBMI. MSVC support for the AVX-512 path is not documented (it is gated on __AVX512IFMA__/__AVX512VBMI__ and uses __builtin_unreachable).
Code that relies on std::to_chars' bounded-buffer contract (returns errc::value_too_large instead of overflowing), or that needs bases other than 10, 8/16/32-bit types or floating point.

Projects that need a mature dependency: version 0.1.0, 22 commits all between 2026-05-03 and 2026-05-19, no tagged release, no CI workflow in the library repo, and the one outside PR (#7, RISC-V fallback, 2026-06-19) is unmerged.

integration.dependencies: none (C++17 standard library only; CMake 3.14+ for the provided build, single source file src/simditoa.cpp)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; the fast path needs a GCC or Clang that accepts -mavx512f -mavx512dq -mavx512bw -mavx512vl -mavx512ifma -mavx512vbmi (benchmarked with Ubuntu 22.04's GCC 11, derived from the public scripts)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512 IFMA + VBMI (Ice Lake and later Intel, Zen 4 and later AMD) for the SIMD path; any platform with the portable scalar fallback
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the functions are stateless (constexpr tables, no global mutable state in the source), so concurrent calls on separate buffers are safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same job as integer std::to_chars, but the signature is to_chars(value, char*) returning a length, with no end pointer or error code, base 10 only and int64_t/uint64_t only, so call sites must be rewritten and buffers sized to 21 bytes

gotchas: Buffer contract: to_chars_homogeneous does full-width 16-byte stores, writing up to 16 bytes from the start of the buffer even for a 9-digit number (the extra bytes are zeros). Appending into a larger output buffer therefore clobbers whatever follows the digits unless 21 bytes of slack are reserved; the default heterogeneous path uses masked stores and writes only the digits. The usage comment in include/simditoa.h names simditoa::MAX_INT64_CHARS, which does not exist; the constant is MAX_DIGITS.

Benchmark presentation, not code: RESULTS.md's prose and tables were written by OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini and mislabel columns (the 'UNIFORM_POS' column holds FIXED:1 data, and the 219M headline geomean mixes the homogeneous and heterogeneous variants); the README's 194.8M and 269.7M figures come from an earlier LLM summary. Use the raw google/benchmark output. Recomputed from it, the default heterogeneous path has a realistic-subset geomean of 176.0M vs std::to_chars 62.5M (2.82x), with yy_itoa next at 136.3M (derived from page data).

No harness defect found that favours simditoa: every contender uses the same 1M pre-generated values, the same 32-byte stack buffer with DoNotOptimize, and the same global AVX-512 flags. simditoa is linked as a separate static library, so each call is out of line (no LTO), while std::to_chars is inlined from the header. Two limits remain: only one CPU (Sapphire Rapids) and one standard library (GCC 11 libstdc++) were measured, and the library was fetched at GIT_TAG main, so the exact commit measured is not recorded.

The single-value numbers are throughput of independent conversions in a tight loop. With per-element output buffers (batch sweep) the realistic geomean is 186.1M vs 58.0M (3.21x), but to_chars_batch on UNIFORM_POS (158.6M) is slower than single calls (186.2M). The tests (basic_test.cpp: edge cases, powers of 10, 100,000 random values, buffer isolation) only exercise the AVX-512 path when built with the flags; a Python model of the 8-digit IFMA formula matched exact digits on 700,000 inputs in this review.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over jeaiii/itoa, {fmt}'s format_int or the SSE2 (Mula) itoa when most values have 9-19 digits and you control the deployment CPU (AVX-512 IFMA): in the same run jeaiii reaches 127.6M and fmt 83.4M ints/s realistic geomean against 176.0M. Pick jeaiii/itoa, which is header-only, portable and 1,011M ints/s at 1 digit, for short or mixed-small numbers or portable builds, and std::to_chars or Boost.Charconv when you need bounds-checked output.
verified_claims_summary: In the author's separate google/benchmark repo (1,000,000 int64 values per distribution, 10 repetitions, max-throughput aggregate, -O3 plus AVX-512 IFMA/VBMI flags, Ubuntu 22.04 GCC 11 libstdc++, GCP c3-standard-8 with Xeon Platinum 8481C), the default simditoa::to_chars converts 176.0M ints/s vs 62.5M for std::to_chars over UNIFORM_POS, LOG_HEAVY and FIXED:12/16/19 (2.82x geomean; 3.1-3.4x at 18-19 digits). It loses at 1-4 digits and on random-sign int64 to yy_itoa (derived from page data).
status_note: The library is new and small (version 0.1.0, written by one author in May 2026 with some AI co-authored commits, no release tags and no activity since 2026-05-19) but MIT OR Apache-2.0 and one source file, so it is easy to vendor. No correctness or harness defect was found behind the numbers; the RESULTS.md and README summaries are LLM-written and mislabelled, so quote the raw output.
